 Advocacy Alert – November 16, 2026
 In this Alliance Advocacy Alert:
 Museums Advocacy Day Registration is OPEN
 What the Mid-Term Elections Mean for Museums
 Legislative Update: Appropriations and Historic Preservation Section 106
 Advocacy Tip of the Month: Start Planning Your Advocacy for 2027
 Museums Advocacy Day Registration Is Open
 With 17 new Senators and more than 100 new House members, we have an opportunity to make gains for the museum field when the new Congress begins in January. In addition to the new members, there will also be significant changes on key Congressional committees.
 Help us reach as many members of Congress as possible by joining us for Museums Advocacy Day, February 22-23, 2027 in Washington, DC. AAM will provide advocacy training and schedule all of your Congressional meetings. View the Schedule-at-a-Glance , book your hotel room at the AAM group rate, watch a previously recorded webinar on what it is like to participate in Museums Advocacy Day, and register .
 Register Today 
 NEW! Scholarship/Travel Stipend : Are you interested in attending Museums Advocacy Day but need financial support to get to Washington, DC? Our new scholarship program provides a $1,000 travel stipend, one year of AAM membership, and complimentary registration for those from underrepresented states or with financial barriers to attend Museums Advocacy Day. Apply by November 30, 2026. 
 Learn more and apply 
 Help make Museums Advocacy Day a success and continue to keep registration rates low! 
 For organizations and associations , AAM has numerous supporter level options from as low as $175. View the options here .
 Interested in becoming a corporate sponsor? Contact us at CorporatePartnerships (at) aam-us.org to learn about corporate sponsorship opportunities.
 You can support Museums Advocacy Day by making a donation .
 What do the Mid-Term Elections Mean for Museums?
 The American Alliance of Museums looks forward to working with the newly elected Congress to increase federal funding for museums and advance policies that strengthen their ability to serve their communities. We welcome the opportunity to build relationships with new members and continue working with returning lawmakers across party lines to make museums a national priority.
 Read the full AAM Statement 
 As we look forward to what the new 120th Congress will bring, please make sure to join the AAM Government Relations and Advocacy team on December 2 at 2:00pm ET for a webinar to learn more about the election results and what they could mean for the museum field.
 Register for the “What’s Next? Post 2026 Election Round Up” Webinar 
 Legislative Update: Appropriations and Historic Preservation Section 106
 Appropriations : The current Continuing Resolution (CR) that is funding the federal government at Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) levels expires on December 11, 2026. Congress will be considering its options over the next few weeks. The most likely scenarios are either another short-term CR that goes into the start of the new Congress or a full year CR that covers the entire Fiscal Year 2027 that would end on September 30, 2027. A CR is a bill that funds the government at current levels for a specified amount of time. While a CR of some sort is the most likely option for the December 11th deadline, it is still possible that Congress does pass one or more of the individual appropriations bills.
 Last week, the Senate did release its version of seven of the twelve individual appropriations bills, one of which was the Interior Appropriations Bill. This is the bill that contains funding for the National Endowment for the Arts (NEA) and National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH). The Senate bill proposes funding NEA and NEH at the current FY26 levels. This is an improvement over the House version of the bill, which had proposed a significant decrease. Congress still needs to negotiation on the differences between the House and Senate bills, which is why a CR in some form is the most likely scenario for the December 11th deadline. Note, the Senate has not yet released its version of the appropriations bill that contains funding for the Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS).
 Write to Encourage Congress to Support IMLS Funding 
 Write to Encourage Congress to Support NEH and NEA Funding 
 Historic Preservation Section 106 : The Senate is currently considering a larger bill on project permitting that includes harmful changes to the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) Section 106. In addition, there is still a possible OMB proposed rule that could be released anytime that would gut Section 106.
 Over the summer, AAM joined over 600 organizations in signing a letter calling on Congress to reject the efforts to gut Section 106, which requires federal agencies to consider the impacts a project has on historic properties and places, and consider mitigation to limit damage. This process allows for the public, local governments, and tribal communities to weigh in with their local expertise. Of particular concern are proposals that would reduce or eliminate the opportunity for the public, state and local governments, and Tribal communities to weigh in on the matter. Write your members of Congress today expressing your concerns over proposed changes to Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.
 Write to Congress Expressing Concerns Over Changes to Section 106 
 Advocacy Tip of the Month: Start Planning Your Advocacy for 2027
 Now is the time to start thinking about your advocacy efforts for 2027. Will you have community events, ribbon cuttings, or new exhibit openings that you can invite them to? Are you able to attend Museums Advocacy Day or a state museum/arts/humanities advocacy day? Will you meet with them in one of their local offices? With so many new members of Congress, new members of state legislators, and new governors, there are a lot of opportunities to build and foster relationships.
